messages.content: As a chatbot, I need to identify the correct intent for a set of user queries. Can you assist me in determining the appropriate intent for each of these queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there], using the predefined intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]? Please send a GET request to the intent recognition service's URL with these queries.

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the data as a response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The complete URL to which the GET request will be sent. It should be in the format 'http://www.example.com/path'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries from a predefined list of intents. Each intent code should be a string.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a floating-point number. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: A user agent string identifying the client software, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary containing HTTP headers to send along with the request.

message.content: Sure! To accurately map those phrases to their corresponding intent‑codes via your intent‑recognition service, I’ll need the exact endpoint URL where the service expects its requests. Once you provide that, I can make a proper GET call including all four queries so it returns the recognized intents for each one.

We can use the `functions.get_response` tool. Provide url (maybe placeholder). Since not known, but we could construct e.g., "http://example-intent-service.com/analyze" or similar. [hello -> hello]
[I want to transfer funds -> transfer_funds]
[show my balance -> get_balance]
[hey there] ambiguous but likely hello.

But they explicitly asked to send GET request. Might interpret that we should attempt to call an example service. Let's create a hypothetical URL: "https://api.intentrecognitionservice.com/v1/intents". We'll pass queries param as JSON array encoded. Use header Accept application/json.

Let's craft payload: {queries:["hello", ...]} but GET can't include body. So encode as query parameters: ?q[]=hello&q[]=I%20want...

We'll produce a single request with all queries. Then parse result.
